items.title: Radiology scores over $1B through No Surprises Act’s independent dispute-resolution process - Radiology Business
items.reason: This item reports on outcomes from the No Surprises Act's Independent Dispute Resolution (IDR) process, a core component of the Act's implementation that directly affects revenue-cycle operations and reimbursement strategies.
items.summary: Radiology practices have recovered over $1 billion through the No Surprises Act's Independent Dispute Resolution (IDR) process, which allows providers to challenge payer denials and reimbursement decisions when payments fall below expected rates. This significant aggregate outcome demonstrates the IDR mechanism's material impact on provider revenue recovery in the radiology specialty. The IDR process, a key feature of NSA implementation, enables revenue-cycle teams to pursue disputed claims outside of traditional appeals, making this milestone relevant to understanding the financial implications of NSA enforcement for healthcare providers.

items.title: Monogram Health to pay $2.4M to settle Medicare Advantage upcoding allegations
items.reason: This reports a settlement involving Medicare Advantage payers (Cigna and Humana) and allegations of upcoding/fraud, which falls directly under payer enforcement actions and claims-denial/downcoding litigation within the rubric.
items.summary: Monogram Health, a home health company, has agreed to pay $2.4 million to settle Justice Department allegations that it overcharged Medicare Advantage plans operated by Cigna and Humana by inflating diagnostic codes. The settlement addresses upcoding claims involving claims submitted to these major payers under their Medicare Advantage contracts. This regulatory enforcement action is significant for revenue-cycle teams because it demonstrates DOJ focus on coding accuracy and payer audit scrutiny of home health billing practices, particularly under MA contracts, and signals increased risk for similar investigations across the industry.
